claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys have high saturation magnetization and coercive fields below 100 Oe in as-cast or conventionally annealed conditions.
Heavy cold deformation followed by a brief intermediate-temperature anneal can significantly increase the coercivity of single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys.
High-pressure torsion or severe cold rolling will induce a high density of dislocations and twins.
A brief anneal at approximately 400–500 °C will stabilize nanoscale ordering and residual lattice strains.
The proposed deformation and annealing treatment can retain a single-phase fcc structure without producing a second phase.
Nanometer-scale ordered regions, dislocations, twins, and lattice-strain fields act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
The defect structures and local ordering create internal barriers that impede magnetic domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion raises the coercive field.
Saturation magnetization will remain largely unchanged because the treatment causes no major compositional or phase changes.
The treatment could increase coercivity to several times the untreated baseline and well above 100 Oe.
Heavy deformation may initiate a phase transformation if the deformation boundary is exceeded.
Excessive annealing recovery can eliminate the domain-wall-pinning defects.
The relevant magnetic response should be measured at room temperature using VSM or SQUID magnetometry.
Retention of the fcc phase and creation of nanoscale defects can be evaluated by XRD and TEM.
